name: Acacia binervia
description: A long-lived wattle with blue-green, hairy leaves and rod-shaped bright yellow flower spikes in late winter and spring. It suits most soils, including alkaline ones.
care_note: Its leaves are toxic to livestock.

name: Acacia floribunda
description: A fast-growing small tree with drooping branches and pale yellow flower spikes in winter. It often grows along rivers and lives longer than most wattles, up to about 30 years.

name: Acacia covenyi
description: A tough wattle with striking blue-grey leaves and fragrant golden ball flowers in late winter and spring. It is rare in the wild but easy to buy, and makes a good screen or windbreak.

name: Acacia iteaphylla
description: A shrub with silvery, weeping, willow-like leaves and pale yellow ball flowers. Its young seed pods are silvery too.
care_note: Please check the trunk for borers. It has naturalised in Western Australia and Tasmania, outside its natural range.

name: Acacia pendula
description: An inland tree with hard, fissured grey bark, weeping branches and flowers mainly in summer and autumn.

name: Acacia pycnantha
description: Australia's floral emblem: a fast-growing wattle with masses of fragrant golden ball flowers from late winter into spring. It can be short-lived.
care_note: It has naturalised in Tasmania and Western Australia, outside its natural range.

name: Acacia terminalis
description: A shrub or small tree with soft, fern-like leaves and an unusually long flowering season through the cooler months.

name: Acacia myrtifolia
description: A shrub with red stems and myrtle-like leaves that looks good all year, with ball flowers in winter and spring. Some forms are almost prostrate.
pruning: Prune lightly after flowering to keep it bushy.

name: Crinum pedunculatum
description: A large bulbous perennial with broad strappy leaves and clusters of white, highly fragrant flowers on tall stems from late spring to early autumn. It copes with poorly drained clay, shade and coastal sites.
care_note: Slugs and snails attack it, so an iron-based snail bait helps. Please shelter it from wind in coastal gardens.

name: Cupaniopsis anacardioides
description: A small coastal tree with glossy leaves, smooth grey bark and a spreading crown that gives good shade. Green-yellow flowers in spring are followed by decorative orange-yellow seed pods in summer.
care_note: It can grow large, so please plant it away from drains, paths and buildings.

name: Livistona australis
description: A tall fan palm with glossy, fan-shaped leaves on a single trunk and large cream flower sprays. It can be kept in a pot while young.
care_note: The leaf stalks have sharp spines, so please wear thick gloves when clearing old fronds.

name: Wodyetia bifurcata
description: A neat, self-cleaning palm from the Cape Melville Range in far north Queensland, with dense, feathery fronds on a grey trunk. It suits tropical and subtropical gardens.

toxic.note: The ripe red fruit is poisonous. Please keep children from eating it.

name: Alocasia brisbanensis
description: A massive rainforest herb, 1 to 1.8 metres high, with very large leaves on a thick stem, green lily-like flowers in early summer and red fruit. It suits shady, damp spots around pools and ponds.

name: Poa poiformis
description: A dense tussock grass from coastal cliffs, dunes and estuaries with fine, weeping leaves. Selections such as 'Kingsdale' have dark green foliage and suit borders and rockeries.
care_note: It dislikes high humidity.

name: Melaleuca bracteata
description: A shrub or tree from inland watercourses with hard, fissured bark and small white flowers in spring and summer. Golden and green selections such as 'Revolution Gold' make dense screens and windbreaks.
pruning: It responds well to pruning, which keeps it dense.

name: Epacris impressa
description: An open shrub with masses of tubular bell flowers in pink, red or white from autumn to spring, at their best in winter. Honeyeaters feed on them.
care_note: It needs moist, well-drained, slightly acid soil.

name: Hakea multilineata
description: A large shrub or small tree with long, grass-like leaves and bright pink flower spikes in winter and spring that feed honeyeaters.
care_note: It suits places with low summer humidity. In humid areas it can collapse suddenly, so a grafted plant is recommended there.

name: Eucalyptus pauciflora
description: A slow-growing, long-lived gum of cold sites, with twisted branches and smooth white, grey or yellow bark that sheds in ribbons. White flowers appear in spring and summer, and it is a good honey source.

name: Eucalyptus ovata
description: A tall gum of low, permanently damp ground, with rough grey-black bark on the lower trunk and smooth white, pink or yellow bark above that sheds in long ribbons.

name: Grevillea victoriae
description: A grevillea of rocky mountain slopes, from low and spreading to 4 metres tall, flowering chiefly in spring and summer.

name: Banksia marginata
description: A very variable banksia, usually a shrub about 2 metres high, with leaves dark green above and silver beneath and pale yellow flower spikes. Dwarf forms such as 'Minimarg' suit low hedges and rockeries.
pruning: Pruning after flowering makes it denser.
care_note: Please avoid waterlogged ground.

name: Bursaria spinosa
description: An upright, prickly shrub with dense heads of sweetly scented, creamy-white flowers around Christmas. Its prickly branches shelter small birds, and its flowers are an important nectar source for butterflies.

name: Patersonia sericea
description: A tufted plant with narrow leaves and deep blue or purple, iris-like flowers in spring and summer. Each flower lasts a day, but new ones open over a long season.

name: Senna artemisioides
description: A silvery shrub from the arid inland with narrow grey leaves and small clusters of bright yellow flowers in spring and summer. The usual garden form grows about 1.5 metres tall.
care_note: It needs full sun and good drainage.

name: Chamelaucium uncinatum
description: An open shrub from Western Australia with aromatic, narrow leaves and pink waxy flowers from late winter into summer. It is a popular cut flower.
pruning: Light pruning after flowering keeps it dense.
care_note: It does best where summers are dry and is not recommended for the humid tropics. Please give it good drainage, such as a raised bed.

name: Agonis flexuosa
description: A graceful tree with weeping foliage from coastal south-west Western Australia, with small white flowers along the branches in spring and summer. Compact and dark-leaved forms make good screens.
pruning: It responds well to pruning and can be clipped to shape.
care_note: It is prone to myrtle rust in warm areas.

name: Hardenbergia comptoniana
description: A vigorous twining climber from south-west Western Australia with glossy dark green leaves and masses of purple pea flowers in spring. It also makes a groundcover that holds banks together.
pruning: Trim after flowering if it needs tidying.
care_note: It has occasionally naturalised outside Western Australia.

name: Melaleuca nesophila
description: A dense shrub from the south coast of Western Australia with pale purple pompom flowers from spring through summer. It is drought tolerant and adaptable.

name: Blechnum cartilagineum
description: A hardy tufted fern up to a metre tall whose new fronds are pink and mature to green. It tolerates frost and drought once settled.
care_note: It prefers a sheltered spot out of full sun, in moist soil rich in organic matter.

name: Stenocarpus sinuatus
description: A rainforest tree with glossy leaves and striking red flowers arranged like the spokes of a wheel. It grows smaller in gardens and in cooler places.

name: Vitex rotundifolia
description: A spreading coastal groundcover or low shrub with grey-green leaves and blue or purple flowers in any month. It roots as it spreads and can cover 3 to 4 metres.

name: Eremophila nivea
description: A shrub with silvery, silky leaves and purple tubular flowers from winter through summer. It suits dry climates and is short-lived in humid areas, where grafted plants do better.
care_note: It needs good drainage and full sun, and mounding the soil helps.

name: Eremophila glabra
description: A very variable emu bush, from prostrate forms to shrubs 3 metres tall, with grey-green leaves and red, orange or yellow tubular flowers from autumn through summer.

name: Eremophila polyclada
description: A large, open emu bush with big pale mauve to white flowers spotted brown in the throat, mainly in summer but at any time of year. It drops its leaves in drought to save water, and birds and insects visit the flowers.
care_note: It dislikes humidity and poor drainage.

name: Carpobrotus glaucescens
description: A creeping succulent from coastal sand dunes with long trailing stems that root as they go, thick triangular leaves and large deep pink-purple flowers from October to January.

name: Cymbopogon ambiguus
description: A fast-growing clumping grass with blue-grey, lemon-scented leaves and fluffy silvery flower heads. The leaves release their scent when brushed and can be made into tea.
pruning: Cutting back the old leaves brings fresh growth.
care_note: It self-seeds but is not invasive.

name: Xanthostemon chrysanthus
description: A rainforest tree from north Queensland with dense trusses of golden flowers in summer and autumn that feed nectar-eating birds and insects. It stays smaller in gardens than in the wild.
care_note: In cooler areas it grows less vigorously and may flower erratically.

name: Syzygium smithii
description: A hardy, dense lilly pilly with glossy leaves and fluffy cream flowers in spring and summer. It reaches 8 to 10 metres in gardens, and compact forms such as 'Minor' make good hedges.

name: Brachychiton populneus
description: A highly drought-tolerant tree with a dense canopy of glossy leaves, long planted for shade and stock fodder. It tolerates pruning to limit its size.

name: Hibiscus heterophyllus
description: A medium to large open shrub with prickly stems and large hibiscus flowers, each lasting a day or two while new ones keep opening.

name: Cordyline stricta
description: A tall, narrow plant with long, glossy, deep green leaves and clusters of small white to purple flowers in winter and spring, followed by black berries.
care_note: Frost can damage it in colder areas, but it usually recovers.

name: Melaleuca lateritia
description: An upright shrub from damp shrubland in south-west Western Australia with bright red to orange bottlebrush flowers. It copes with humid east-coast summers better than most western species.
pruning: A light prune each year keeps it bushy.

name: Enchylaena tomentosa
description: A small, very drought-tolerant shrub, upright or prostrate, with sweet and salty berries that ripen from green to red. It grows on saline soil, dunes and saltmarsh.

name: Rhagodia spinescens
description: A hardy saltbush with silvery leaves and a dense habit that makes an informal low hedge. It tolerates frost, drought and salt, so it suits coastal sites.
pruning: It can be pruned to shape.

name: Thryptomene saxicola
description: A small spreading shrub with tiny aromatic leaves and masses of small flowers, mainly in spring. It is a tough, drought-tolerant plant and a long-lasting cut flower.

name: Geijera parviflora
description: A slow-growing small tree from inland Australia with drooping foliage that is strongly scented when crushed. It is very drought tolerant and is planted for shade and stock feed. Its cream, musky-scented flowers can attract blowflies.

name: Curcuma australasica
description: A tropical clumping plant from Cape York with long, light green leaves and yellow summer flowers set in pink bracts. It dies back to its rhizome in the dry season.
care_note: In southern Australia it needs a heated greenhouse.
